evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'we just need to ask you a few questions to get you on the right track this would take about five to ten minutes every time then you can be able to build an accurate you can depend on sounds good' — framing is present but rushed; rep doesn't clearly wait for a yes before moving forward into probing.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Name (Nicholas), moving day (tomorrow), route (5308 to 3615 W. Walnut Hill, Irving Texas), and size (1200 sq ft apartment, two bedroom) all extracted during the call.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Rep covers: property type (apartment), floor/stories (third floor at both locations), number of rooms (two bedroom), walking distance (ten minutes from origin, ten feet from destination), access concerns (stairs, no elevators), box count (twenty boxes). All seven logistics items addressed.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks: 'with the total number of boxes. Is it still between 25 to 35 boxes, twenty boxes.' Customer confirms twenty boxes.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides: 'a typical two bedroom apartment normally takes two movers that's between three and a half to five and a half hours' (anchor), then personalizes to this specific move: 'we're coming from a two bedroom appointment located on the third floor going to the new location which is less than fifteen minutes away... two movers and one truck estimated time is between five to six hours, the estimated cost in case they end up six hours would be $1,224.'
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses: '$102 per hour per mover,' 'everything is already included... gas trucks, taxes and insurance, all the wraps deposit, the bonds,' and 'no hidden fees of any type.' Also notes: 'you only need to pay once the job is done and only for the actual hours' (time-based, not a fixed guess). Both transparency and the 'not a guess' commitment present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep never asks 'does that feel fair?' After stating the estimate, rep immediately pivots: 'And we can be able to book your spot as early as 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM...' No pause or check-in on fairness.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'we still have on time guarantee.' No discount terms mentioned (what happens if late, when discounting starts). Framing is present but vague on the specific guarantee terms.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep says: 'we will also provide up to $2,000 per move that has to repair, replace and reimburse for your items' and 'no hidden fees of any type.' The $2,000 coverage is stated and the no-hidden-fees framing covers the no-deductible/no-fine-print intent. Fully delivered.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask 'does that put those to rest?' or any equivalent closing check on the Two Promises. No confirmation that the customer feels assured by the guarantees.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep never asks 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final concerns probe. Moves directly to: 'would you like our help with your move for tomorrow?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep never asks 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' or equivalent catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks: 'would you like our help with your move for tomorrow?' Customer appears confused, rep rephrases: 'Would you like to block that in and reserve the movers for tomorrow in the morning?' Both are plain asks with no softened out; customer says 'Yeah' and moves to confirmation.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No statement about rate lock or guarantee that the quoted price holds.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Rep confirms: date (tomorrow morning), phone number (verified 8-502-660-3335), arrival window (8:30 AM to 9:00 AM, though customer initially asked for afternoon and was offered 12 PM; final booking is morning). Rep does NOT confirm addresses at the end, crew size (two movers), or leave notes for crew about customer concerns. Partially confirmed.

top_strength: Rep systematically gathered all seven logistics details (property type, floors, rooms, walking distance, access concerns, box count, additional stops) and correctly anchored the estimate to a typical range before personalizing it to the customer's specific move.
coaching_note: Section 2 (Their Agenda) was skipped entirely—rep never asked 'Other than price, what are your biggest concerns about this move?' before diving into probing, which is the highest-value discovery checkpoint on the call card.
